reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals the user picker without validating the passcode. The sign-in POST also omits the required anti-forgery header.

findingList.message: The passcode step does not validate the passcode before revealing the seeded users, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the passcode is nonempty, then requests /api/auth/users without sending or validating it.
evidence.failureScenario: A user enters a wrong passcode and /api/auth/users returns 200; the page reveals the seeded-user picker before any successful passcode step. The wrong passcode is rejected only after the user selects someone and submits sign-in.

findingList.message: The state-changing sign-in request omits the anti-forgery header required by the acceptance criterion (OWASP A01:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only the Content-Type header; the anti-forgery token is stored only after this request succeeds.
evidence.failureScenario: If the server requires the specified anti-forgery header for state-changing requests, the sign-in POST lacks it and is rejected, so the user cannot sign in.

reviewers.summary: The passcode is not validated before the user picker appears, and the sign-in POST lacks the required anti-forgery header. The accessibility criterion also has no tests for keyboard operation or control labels.

findingList.message: The passcode step does not validate the passcode before revealing the seeded-user picker, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the field is nonempty, then requests /api/auth/users without sending the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: A user enters an incorrect passcode; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, the picker appears before any successful passcode check.

findingList.message: The sign-in POST omits the required anti-forgery header (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control), despite the criterion requiring it on every state-changing request.

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header; the CSRF token is set in client state only after the response.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the anti-forgery header for this state-changing request, submitting the sign-in form is rejected because the request has no token.

findingList.message: The third acceptance criterion lacks tests for keyboard operation and labels; add tests that fail when either behavior is broken.

evidence.codePathTraced: The tests cover focus movement and sign-out behavior, but none exercises keyboard-only operation or verifies that every control has an accessible label.
evidence.failureScenario: If a control becomes unreachable by keyboard or loses its label, the current tests still pass, leaving the keyboard-operability and labeling behavior in the third acceptance criterion unverified.

reviewers.summary: The picker request occurs before any passcode validation, so the seeded roster can be disclosed to unauthenticated visitors. The later sign-in request may reject access, but it cannot undo that disclosure.

findingList.message: The user list is exposed before the passcode is validated, contrary to the sign-in gate. This is an unauthorized disclosure of account metadata (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode handler checks only that the field is nonempty, then requests /api/auth/users without sending the passcode and displays the returned users.
evidence.failureScenario: An unauthenticated visitor enters any nonempty value and receives the seeded users' names and roles before the sign-in endpoint checks the passcode.
